newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish one-year bond min price seen down at tender.
newsitem.headline: Polish one-year bond min price seen down at tender.

text.p: The minimum price of Polish one-year index-linked bonds is seen falling at Tuesday's 200 million zloty primary tender, analysts said on Monday.

They said demand was likely to match the ministry's offer but investors were expected to bid for lower prices after recent increases of money market rates and cuts in the public offer price of Poland's one-year bond.
"Demand may match the offer, but many investors will likely bid at a deep discount," said Piotr Dalkowski from Pioneer Investment Fund in Warsaw.

Analysts said the bond, whose coupon is the cumulated inflation rate of 12 months ending in December 1997, would be attractive with at around 93.5, giving a return of around 20 percent against a 52-week T-bill yield of 19.94 percent.
They said the bonds should be discounted because of their low liquidity, but added that the finance ministry was not likely to accept bids below 95.00.
At the last auction of the similar bonds in November 1996 the minimum price was 96.67 and the average price was 96.74.
The value date for this auction is on February 3, 1997.
The next auction of these bonds, maturing on March 4, 1998, is sheduled on February 25, 1997.
